$comment: Canonical dataset for the auspol tracker. See polls.schema.json for field meanings. Edit this file to add a poll, then run: node .build/newtracker/build.mjs

essentialBackfill.note: Essential 2007-2019 backfill. CSV report dates re-keyed onto the preceding Sunday (fieldwork end); `oth` reconstructed as the 100-minus-residual the CSVs omitted; waves already in the file were skipped, not overwritten. cyclePolls.2010 / cycleApproval.2007 hold the 2007-2010 term, which no CYC_META entry charts - stored so one can be.

Essential.note: Essential's published 2PP is undecided-inclusive, so the pair sums to <100 rather than 100. The build reads that shortfall as the poll's undecided share after preferences, so it is a fact with a consumer now, not just an exemption.

release.note: Roy Morgan files its weekly federal voting-intention release on a Monday, about 4.30pm eastern. Stated from the house’s schedule rather than measured, because its release URLs are an unreliable witness: the early ones are named for the fieldwork end (a Sunday) rather than the post, so the slug weekday reads Monday in only two thirds of the full record while the last twelve are Monday eleven times.

One wave per calendar month, on no discernible day of it: five consecutive months Apr–Aug 2026, landing on the 17th, 22nd, 22nd, 13th and 24th. Measured as an interval the median's ± spills past the month's ends (13 Sep–5 Oct for the Sep 2026 slot), which the house's own rhythm rules out, so the calendar month is the window.

Fox & Hedgehog.note: Four waves, last 26 May 2026, silent since. Flagged by hand so its slot does not sit red on Next expected polls indefinitely; unflag if it resumes.

Freshwater.note: Five waves, last 15 May 2026, silent since. Flagged by hand so its slot does not sit red on Next expected polls indefinitely; unflag if it resumes.

events.label: Sussan Ley becomes Liberal leader
events.desc: Ley replaces Peter Dutton as Leader of the Liberal Party and Opposition Leader after the 2025 election loss.

events.label: First Coalition dissolution
events.desc: The Liberal–National Coalition dissolves for the first time, weeks after the 2025 election defeat.

events.label: Barnaby Joyce quits the Nationals
events.desc: Joyce resigns from the National Party to sit as an Independent.

events.label: Barnaby Joyce joins One Nation
events.desc: Joyce defects to One Nation – the first sitting MP defection from the major-party bloc to ONP.

events.label: Bondi Beach shooting
events.desc: A shooting at Bondi Beach in Sydney.

events.label: Coalition dissolves again
events.desc: Second dissolution of the Liberal–National Coalition.

events.label: Angus Taylor becomes Liberal leader
events.desc: Replaces Sussan Ley as Leader of the Liberal Party and Opposition Leader.

events.label: Strait of Hormuz closed
events.desc: Closure during Iran war triggers an Australian fuel crisis.

events.label: Canavan leads the Nationals
events.desc: Matt Canavan replaces David Littleproud as National Party leader.

events.label: One Nation wins Farrer
events.desc: One Nation gains Farrer from the Liberals – the party's first lower-house seat won at a by-election.

events.label: 2026 federal Budget
events.desc: Treasurer Jim Chalmers delivers the Albanese government’s fifth federal budget, rated, according to Newspoll, as the worst for the economy since 1993.
